body:
New York: US pharma major, Pfizer announced a strategic co-funding agreement with Blackstone, securing up to $1.5 billion in development costs for its investigational monthly GLP-1 molecule berobenatide, through 2028.

Under the agreement, the alternative asset manager will be eligible to receive milestone-based payments over multiple years, while Pfizer retains full operational control and decision-making authority over the drug's development.

After shelving its Danuglipron program, Pfizer is attempting a second bout with several multi-billion dollar bets in the booming anti-obesity segment. It acquired berobenatide under its $10 billion takeover of Metsera last year.

The first major deal under the new CFO Cecile Guegan comes at a time when Pfizer’s stock is struggling to find its footing on Wall Street amid its push to reignite growth post 2028 through new product launches in oncology and obesity.

Berobenatide is termed an ultra-long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist which leans on less frequent dosing to hedge against competing therapies from Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk, which are administered weekly.

Pfizer has lined up 10 late-stage trials for the monthly shot this year. The drug demonstrated up to 16 per cent weight-loss in a phase 2b study (VESPER-1 ) after 32 weeks of treatment.

“Today’s announcement helps us advance our comprehensive obesity program and maintain the financial capacity and flexibility to invest in our broader pipeline across all therapeutic areas,” said Cecile Guegan, CFO, Pfizer.

“We are pleased to support the broad and rigorous development of berobenatide as the anchor of Pfizer’s cardiometabolic pipeline,” Dr Nicholas Galakatos, Global Head of Blackstone Life Sciences, added.
